canonical_topic: Seasonal Demand Regime Shift Risk in Gas Storage Valuation
definition: A storage valuation built on historical seasonal price/demand patterns is exposed to the risk that those patterns shift permanently as the underlying drivers of gas demand evolve.
core_idea: As new sources of demand emerge over time, the seasonal price pattern a storage strategy assumes can change structurally, undermining valuations based on older historical patterns.
key_points: Example: in the mid-1980s there were very few natural-gas-fired power plants, so summer gas demand (and prices) were low relative to winter, heating-driven demand.
Roughly 25 years of natural-gas power plant buildout added a major new source of summer gas demand.
As a result, summer natural gas prices rose sharply, changing the seasonal pattern older storage valuations may have relied on.
relationships: A risk factor for the same seasonal trade described in the Natural Gas Storage Arbitrage Bid Strategy example.
